title: Giving or obtaining developer access in Gitlab
date_basis: Page explicitly says last updated 28 May 2026; date describes the inspected document revision, not the original adoption of the AI rule.
verification_scope: Official developer-access rules, especially rule 8, and displayed revision date; read through web retrieval.
summary: GIMP rejects generative-AI contributions including code, images and text. Its developer-access rules expressly prohibit quietly adding generated material after obtaining push rights.
limitations: Contribution policy, not a productivity or quality experiment. It expressly does not regulate contributors' activities elsewhere. The revision date does not establish when the prohibition began.

title: NetBSD Commit Guidelines
date_basis: Taylor R Campbell's official mailing-list message dated 15 May 2024 records adding the LLM clause to these guidelines: https://mail-index.netbsd.org/netbsd-bugs/2024/05/15/msg083089.html. Current page inspected 13 October 2026.
verification_scope: Official tainted-code clause and dated project mailing-list confirmation; web retrieval.
summary: NetBSD presumes LLM-generated code to be tainted and prohibits committing it without prior written approval from core.
limitations: Not an exceptionless ban on all AI use: prior written core approval is explicitly possible. The licensing presumption is the project's position, not an independent legal conclusion or measured harm.

title: Code of Conduct
date_basis: Current policy inspected 13 October 2026; this page supplies no publication date. A dated 11 July 2025 historical contributing-page revision documents earlier restrictions but does not date this expanded text.
verification_scope: Official scope and Strict No LLM / No AI section, read through web retrieval.
summary: Zig's designated development spaces prohibit LLM-generated code and prose, paraphrasing, editing, translation, shared brainstorming results and LLM-assisted bug finding.
limitations: Applies to the ziglang Codeberg organization, project IRC and development Zulip, not every independent community or project using Zig. No measured productivity effect follows from the rule.
version_note: Historical policy evidence: https://github.com/ziglang/zig/wiki/Contributing/61aff1ce9b3ebd8c38c0f5a18db00c06f0fa4022 (11 July 2025). Do not attribute all current restrictions to that historical revision.

title: Contributing to Redox
date_basis: GitHub file history: cited revision 03d6b8bc05bab7cf03490671cd3d23571214a720 committed 3 September 2026. This is a later document revision, not policy adoption.
verification_scope: Official repository contribution terms and AI Policy section; web text and GitHub history API.
summary: Redox rejects LLM-generated contributions, including issues, merge requests and descriptions. Clearly labeled generated submissions are closed; attempts to circumvent the policy can result in a ban.
limitations: Project governance evidence, not a causal study. Does not show that every AI-assisted activity is detectable or measure the rule's effects.

title: Generative AI (LLM) Policy
date_basis: Official live page inspected 13 October 2026; original publication/adoption date not established. June 2025 board discussion is not treated as proof of adoption.
verification_scope: Entire official policy, including material contributions, trace interpretation and enforcement examples; web retrieval.
summary: Asahi broadly forbids generative-AI tooling for material contributions, citing ethical concerns and possible contamination of clean-room reverse engineering. Its examples include generated issues and LLM interpretation of hardware traces.
limitations: Broader than a generated-code ban, but scoped to material project contributions. Stated ethical and legal concerns are project judgments, not independently established legal findings or experimental outcomes.

title: Kernel Guidelines for Tool-Generated Content
date_basis: Repository revision d699a5da103942fdc0a8a5383359bdec01fc19dd committed 22 July 2026; date describes the cited documentation revision, not the start of AI use in Linux.
verification_scope: Official policy purpose, scope, disclosure and maintainer discretion; web retrieval and GitHub file history API.
summary: Linux accommodates tool-generated contributions under human understanding, DCO responsibility, transparent provenance and testing. Individual maintainers may still reject them, apply additional scrutiny or lower their priority.
limitations: A conditional framework, not blanket acceptance or proof of productivity gains. Trivial typing, formatting and mechanical edits are outside this document's main scope.

title: AI Coding Assistants
date_basis: Cited repository snapshot 72fdff1416e280e2baaa3cca69574defb998437e, merged 20 August 2026; this is a snapshot date, not policy-adoption date or necessarily the last direct file edit.
verification_scope: Official licensing, human sign-off, Assisted-by attribution and bug-validation guidance; web retrieval and GitHub history API.
summary: Kernel guidance makes humans responsible for reviewing and certifying AI-assisted submissions, describes Assisted-by attribution, and asks for reproduction, build/test checks and disclosure of verification limits.
limitations: Guidance documents expected practice, not compliance rates or demonstrated effectiveness. It complements, rather than removes, maintainer discretion to reject generated content.

title: Linus Torvalds "Did What I Preach", Used AI To Make Code Decipherable & Uncovered More Bugs
date_basis: Article's displayed byline and publication date, 12 October 2026.
verification_scope: Public Phoronix article, quoted tag statement and reported merge status; web retrieval. Original kernel tag was not independently retrieved.
summary: Reports Torvalds using LLMs to understand and refactor obscure associative-array code. His quoted statement attributes confirmation of the reported bug and discovery of three additional longstanding bugs to subsequent user-space test-harness execution.
limitations: Secondary account of one episode, with no counterfactual or total-cost measurement. The article says patches were not yet merged to master; do not present them as shipped or attribute all discoveries to the LLM alone.

title: About - Gravity Linux
date_basis: Live FAQ inspected 13 October 2026. Dated introductory blog is 5 September 2026, but does not date this FAQ or the fork itself.
verification_scope: Official About FAQ, especially Gravity Linux vs Asahi Linux; web retrieval.
summary: Gravity's own account says it initially forked from Asahi over policy differences, specifically LLM use, while retaining the shared objective of Linux support on Apple Silicon.
limitations: Self-description establishes the project's stated rationale, not an independent causal history or evidence that the fork improves engineering outcomes. Does not establish the prevalence of such splits.

title: LLM Use and Clean-Room Policy
date_basis: Undated live policy inspected 13 October 2026; adoption date not established.
verification_scope: Official policy sections on permission, human responsibility, contamination, disclosure and process records; web retrieval.
summary: Gravity permits and encourages responsible LLM use while requiring disclosure and demonstrable clean-room provenance. Exposure through an agent can taint the contributor; rewriting proprietary material through an LLM is prohibited.
limitations: Not unconditional acceptance. The project's safeguards and claimed effectiveness are not independently validated; its legal interpretation is not a legal opinion from this review.

title: "We Permit the Use of AI, but [...]": The Landscape of AI Policies in Popular Open Source Projects
verification_scope: arXiv v1 abstract, sampling and detection methods, classification, results and limitations, read as HTML; corpus not independently re-coded.
summary: Among 281 identified policies, 83.3% permit or encourage AI code contributions and 14.9% forbid them; 67.3% require substantial human involvement and 48.8% disclosure.
limitations: Popular active GitHub repositories plus purposively selected prominent projects, restricted to detected policies: not a representative poll of all OSS or a test of policy effectiveness. Detection and manual classification may miss or misclassify rules. Differing samples and detection prevent reading the percentages as a clean trend.
version_note: Extends the earlier 118-policy study; not an independent replication. Under review at TOSEM according to arXiv, not treated as an accepted journal paper.

title: AI Policy, Disclosure, and Human in the Loop: How Are Contribution Guidelines Adapting to GenAI?
verification_scope: arXiv title, authors, abstract, submission/revision dates and conference-acceptance note; result appraisal uses the linked expanded September study.
version_note: First submitted 15 May, revised 13 July 2026; arXiv says accepted to ICSME 2026. Earlier 118-policy study subsequently expanded to 281 policies. Do not count these as independent evidence.

title: You can contribute if you... An Empirical Framework of AI Contribution Policies in OSS
verification_scope: arXiv primary bibliographic identity and abstract checked; full result-level appraisal pending.
version_note: Supporting framework on maintainer attention, accountability, review interactions and newcomer learning. No numerical prevalence or causal effect attributed in the synthesis.
